items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: I was the Tommy Dorsey, you know it was mostly the Dorsey brothers’ library in the book.

ctx.x: So by the time I got to North Texas, that was my third year of college, I had already written extensive big band arrangements for the college band at University of Southern Mississippi. We went to the Mobile Jazz Festival in the spring of ’67 and I met Lou Marini there. And I heard Lou Marini’s charts and I heard him solo. Lou heard my charts and heard me solo. And he says, “Man you should really transfer to North Texas.” So I did. I was 19 years old. I went on the road with the Jimmy Dorsey band. Lee Castle and
the Jimmy Dorsey band. I was the Tommy Dorsey, you know it was mostly the Dorsey brothers’ library in the book. And so I saved up enough money to pay my tuition and first month’s rent.

There’s an anecdote in your bio, or this was an interview you did with somebody, I’m going to read it for a moment: “My first big time gig was playing lead trumpet with Brenda Lee at a club in Jackson, Mississippi. The gig was six nights a week. I always passed out after playing a big, long high C in the middle of the show. I had to hitchhike back and forth to Jackson every night.
